pillars.title: Job training through UMANG
pillars.text: Courses in dress design, beauty and wellness, basic computer skills, Tally accounting and spoken English give young people practical skills and a path to earning their own living. All classes run at NIPUN’s UMANG training centres.
pillars.photo_description: Young women in an UMANG computer class

pillars.title: Hot meals for children
pillars.text: Every child at NIPUN’s education centres gets a freshly cooked, nutritious meal. It fights malnutrition, supports healthy growth and keeps children coming to class.

pillars.title: Local teachers
pillars.text: Vision Builders pays part of the salaries of NIPUN’s teachers, many of whom come from the same communities. It supports their families and builds a learning system the community runs itself.
pillars.photo_description: Trainees and teachers celebrating Navratri at the UMANG centre

pillars.title: Scholarships for girls
pillars.text: The Vision Builders Scholarship supports 25 adolescent girls from Meera Bagh and Nihal Vihar, chosen against clear criteria, so money is not the reason they stop studying.
pillars.photo_description: Girls and women at an art and craft workshop

stories.name: Manisha
stories.text: Manisha moved to Delhi from Bihar and had to leave school when money ran out. She finished Class X through open schooling, then took UMANG’s Beauty and Wellness course in 2025. After working in a salon, she opened her own parlour and now earns ₹15,000–18,000 a month.
stories.photo_description: Manisha outside the beauty parlour she opened

stories.name: Bhawna, 22
stories.text: Bhawna had to stop her studies after Class XII and taught herself stitching from YouTube videos. In April 2026 she joined UMANG’s Self-Employed Tailor course and began sewing for neighbours before she even finished. She now earns ₹6,000–10,000 a month and plans to return to college.
stories.photo_description: A trainee at a sewing machine at the UMANG centre

stories.name: Priya, 24
stories.text: Priya dreamed of being a makeup artist, but her family couldn’t afford training. After UMANG’s Beauty and Wellness course she joined a salon and is earning her first paycheque. Her next goal is to work independently.
